tweets.author: firsthandbitcoin.com
tweets.text:
What died was expensive power, not mining. Those machines kept adding bitcoin through the 2022 crash and the 2024 halving.

Every month, every machine: firsthandbitcoin.com/data/mining...

tweets.author: firsthandbitcoin.com
tweets.text:
The record: 261 monthly machine purchases, 2018 to 2022, every power bill paid, the machine counted at what it sells for now.

On 3.9¢ power, 184 ended with more bitcoin than the same dollars spent on bitcoin. 98% ended with more dollars than went in.

tweets.author: firsthandbitcoin.com
tweets.text:
Here's what that misses. The network resets its difficulty every two weeks.

When weak machines on expensive power switch off, every machine still running earns a bigger share of the same new bitcoin.

Mining doesn't die. It moves to cheap power.

tweets.author: firsthandbitcoin.com
tweets.text:
Every crash and every halving, someone declares bitcoin mining dead.

So we checked every month from 2018 to 2022: a machine bought on 3.9¢ power, against the same dollars put straight into bitcoin.

7 purchases in 10 ended with more bitcoin than buying.
